subject: Day 79: raspberries and squeals
bodyText:
Today's focus
Vocal play is expanding into prolonged cooing, squeals, and the first lip-vibration raspberries. These experiments are the raw material of speech, and your responses are what turn them into conversation.

Action items
- Blow raspberries and trade squeals with him, treating each sound as a turn: make a sound, pause, let him answer, then respond. This back-and-forth pattern predicts stronger later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Keep tracking sleep windows (last wake, time fell asleep, nap length) this week; the pattern stabilizes by about 12 to 14 weeks and gives you a loose schedule to anchor against the coming regression.
- Plan for the first daycare illness, which typically arrives within two to four weeks of starting; have the pediatrician's after-hours line saved and a decision in advance for who stays home.
- Lock in the first-birthday venue now if booking is required, since the calmest week of the quarter is the right time to clear this off the list.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Loud squeals, raspberries, and vocal experiments at all hours; this is healthy vocal-range expansion, not agitation.
- [monitor] Persistent crying that is disproportionate to the daycare handoff, or fisted hands that rarely open; document and raise at the 4-month visit.
- [call within 24h] A first daycare fever, or persistent feeding refusal; under 90 days this still warrants same-day evaluation.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, apnea, blue lips, or labored breathing is a same-day call, and 911 immediately for blue lips or breathing trouble!

Enrichment opportunities
- Turn his raspberries into a rhythm game by echoing them in a sung beat; live, participatory music layered on his own sounds drives communicative and perceptual development. Gerry et al. 2012, active music in infancy: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Read aloud with exaggerated sounds and animal noises and pause to invite imitation; the prosody and the interaction matter more than the book itself. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Keep cumulative tummy time at 75 to 90 minutes in short bouts, placing a toy just out of reach to prompt swiping and reaching as his arms strengthen. AAP HealthyChildren, tummy to play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep consolidation window opens (~3 months); set and hold the sleep-wake routine
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2
- Weeks 14-18: 4-month sleep regression as night wakings increase

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
